description: Apply security hardening to a Windows Server following CIS benchmarks or STIG guidelines.

steps.description: Select the appropriate CIS benchmark or STIG profile for the target Windows Server version and role.

inputs.name: server-role
inputs.desc: Primary role of the server (domain controller, file server, web server, etc.)

outputs.name: benchmark-profile
outputs.desc: Selected CIS or STIG benchmark profile with version

outputs.name: baseline-scan
outputs.desc: Current compliance state against the selected benchmark

process: Identify the Windows Server version and installed roles
Select the matching CIS benchmark or STIG profile
Run a baseline compliance scan and record the starting score

steps.description: Disable unnecessary Windows services and features based on the server role.

inputs.name: server-role
inputs.desc: Server role determining which services are required

outputs.name: disabled-services-list
outputs.desc: List of services and features that were disabled

outputs.name: service-change-log
outputs.desc: Record of each service state change with timestamp

process: List all running services and their startup types
Compare against the benchmark list of required services for this role
Disable each unnecessary service and record the change

steps.description: Configure Windows Firewall rules to allow only required traffic.

inputs.name: server-role
inputs.desc: Server role determining required network ports

inputs.name: benchmark-profile
inputs.desc: CIS or STIG benchmark with firewall requirements

outputs.name: firewall-ruleset
outputs.desc: Applied firewall rules with allow and deny entries

outputs.name: firewall-change-log
outputs.desc: Record of rule changes from the default configuration

process: Enable Windows Firewall on all profiles (domain, private, public)
Configure inbound rules to allow only required ports for the server role
Configure outbound rules and set the default action to block
Test connectivity for required services after applying rules

steps.description: Configure account policies for password complexity, lockout thresholds, and privilege management.

inputs.name: benchmark-profile
inputs.desc: CIS or STIG benchmark with account policy requirements

outputs.name: account-policy-config
outputs.desc: Applied account policy settings

outputs.name: policy-change-log
outputs.desc: Record of each policy change with before and after values

process: Set password complexity requirements (length, character types, history)
Configure account lockout thresholds and duration
Review and restrict local administrator group membership
Configure user rights assignments per the benchmark

steps.description: Configure Windows audit logging to capture security-relevant events.

inputs.name: benchmark-profile
inputs.desc: CIS or STIG benchmark with audit policy requirements

inputs.name: server-role
inputs.desc: Server role to determine role-specific audit categories

outputs.name: audit-policy-config
outputs.desc: Applied audit policy settings by category

outputs.name: log-retention-config
outputs.desc: Event log size and retention settings

process: Configure advanced audit policies for logon events, object access, and privilege use
Set event log maximum sizes and retention method
Configure Sysmon or Windows Event Forwarding if applicable
Verify events are being generated for test actions

steps.description: Remove or disable default accounts and guest access to reduce the attack surface.

inputs.name: benchmark-profile
inputs.desc: CIS or STIG benchmark with account requirements

outputs.name: account-remediation-log
outputs.desc: Record of accounts disabled, renamed, or removed

outputs.name: remaining-accounts
outputs.desc: Final list of active accounts with their roles

process: Disable the Guest account
Rename the built-in Administrator account
Remove unnecessary local accounts and service accounts
Verify that no default or test credentials remain active

steps.description: Run a final compliance scan and produce the Windows Server hardening report.

outputs.name: hardening-report
outputs.desc: Full hardening report with compliance score and remaining exceptions

outputs.name: compliance-score
outputs.desc: Final percentage compliance against the benchmark

process: Run the final compliance scan against the same benchmark
Compare before and after scores
Document any accepted exceptions with justification
Produce the hardening report with the compliance score and change log

description: Apply security hardening to a Linux server following CIS benchmark guidelines.

steps.description: Select and apply the CIS benchmark profile for the target Linux distribution and version.

inputs.name: server-role
inputs.desc: Primary role (web server, database, application, etc.)

outputs.name: benchmark-profile
outputs.desc: Selected CIS benchmark profile

outputs.name: baseline-scan
outputs.desc: Current compliance state before hardening

process: Identify the Linux distribution and version
Select the matching CIS benchmark profile (Level 1 or Level 2)
Run a baseline compliance scan using a tool like OpenSCAP or Lynis

steps.description: Disable unnecessary systemd services and remove unneeded packages.

outputs.name: disabled-services
outputs.desc: List of services stopped and masked

outputs.name: removed-packages
outputs.desc: List of packages removed from the system

process: List all enabled systemd services
Disable and mask services not required for the server role
Remove unnecessary packages (telnet, rsh, talk, etc.)
Verify that required services still function

steps.description: Configure iptables or nftables firewall rules for the server role.

outputs.name: firewall-ruleset
outputs.desc: Applied iptables or nftables rules

outputs.name: firewall-change-log
outputs.desc: Changes made to the firewall configuration

process: Set the default policy to DROP for INPUT and FORWARD chains
Allow established and related connections
Add rules for required inbound ports based on server role
Persist the rules across reboots

steps.description: Harden the SSH configuration to prevent unauthorized access.

outputs.name: ssh-config
outputs.desc: Updated sshd_config with hardened settings

outputs.name: ssh-change-log
outputs.desc: Record of each SSH setting change

process: Disable root login over SSH
Require public key authentication and disable password authentication
Set idle timeout and maximum authentication attempts
Restrict SSH access to specific users or groups
Disable X11 forwarding and agent forwarding unless required

steps.description: Configure auditd rules to monitor security-relevant system activity.

inputs.name: server-role
inputs.desc: Server role for role-specific audit rules

outputs.name: audit-rules
outputs.desc: Applied auditd rules file

outputs.name: audit-config
outputs.desc: Auditd daemon configuration (log size, retention)

process: Install and enable auditd if not already present
Configure rules for file access, privilege escalation, and authentication events
Set log rotation and retention policies
Verify that audit events are being captured for test actions

steps.description: Set filesystem permissions and mount options to restrict unauthorized access.

outputs.name: permission-changes
outputs.desc: Record of permission changes applied

outputs.name: mount-options
outputs.desc: Updated fstab with hardened mount options

process: Set nodev, nosuid, and noexec on /tmp, /var/tmp, and /dev/shm
Set correct ownership and permissions on critical files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, cron directories)
Remove world-writable files and directories or add sticky bits
Check for and remove unowned files

steps.description: Run a final compliance scan and produce the Linux server hardening report.

outputs.name: hardening-report
outputs.desc: Full hardening report with compliance score and remaining items

outputs.name: compliance-score
outputs.desc: Final percentage compliance against the benchmark

process: Run the final compliance scan with the same tool and benchmark
Compare before and after results
Document accepted exceptions with justification
Produce the report with the compliance score and all change logs

description: Harden network devices (routers, switches, firewalls) against unauthorized access and misconfiguration.

steps.description: Disable unused physical and logical ports on network devices.

inputs.name: device-inventory
inputs.desc: List of network devices with model and firmware version

inputs.name: port-usage-map
inputs.desc: Map of which ports are in use and their purpose

outputs.name: disabled-ports-log
outputs.desc: Record of ports shut down or disabled

outputs.name: active-port-list
outputs.desc: Final list of active ports and their assignments

process: Inventory all physical and logical interfaces on each device
Identify ports not connected to any device or service
Administratively shut down unused ports
Assign unused ports to a black-hole VLAN

steps.description: Configure SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption, replacing any SNMPv1 or v2c usage.

inputs.name: device-inventory
inputs.desc: List of network devices to configure

inputs.name: active-port-list
inputs.desc: Active ports for management access planning

outputs.name: snmp-config
outputs.desc: SNMPv3 configuration applied to each device

outputs.name: snmp-change-log
outputs.desc: Record of SNMP version and community string changes

process: Identify current SNMP versions and community strings in use
Create SNMPv3 users with authentication (SHA) and privacy (AES)
Remove SNMPv1 and v2c community strings
Test monitoring connectivity with the new SNMPv3 credentials

steps.description: Configure access control lists to restrict management plane access to authorized hosts.

outputs.name: management-acl
outputs.desc: Applied management access control lists

outputs.name: acl-change-log
outputs.desc: Record of ACL changes per device

process: Define the list of authorized management IP addresses or subnets
Apply ACLs to VTY lines restricting SSH access to authorized hosts
Apply ACLs to SNMP restricting polling to the monitoring server
Test management access from authorized and unauthorized sources

steps.description: Configure centralized syslog logging on all network devices.

inputs.name: management-acl
inputs.desc: Management ACLs ensuring syslog server is reachable

outputs.name: syslog-config
outputs.desc: Syslog configuration applied to each device

outputs.name: log-verification
outputs.desc: Confirmation that log events are arriving at the syslog server

process: Configure each device to send logs to the central syslog server
Set the logging severity level to informational or higher
Include timestamps and source interface in log messages
Verify log arrival at the syslog server with a test event

steps.description: Disable insecure management protocols and replace with secure alternatives.

inputs.name: syslog-config
inputs.desc: Logging configuration to capture protocol changes

outputs.name: protocol-changes
outputs.desc: Record of protocols disabled and their replacements

outputs.name: secure-protocol-config
outputs.desc: Configuration of the secure alternatives

process: Disable Telnet and enable SSH for CLI access
Disable HTTP management and enable HTTPS with a valid certificate
Disable TFTP for config transfers and use SCP or SFTP
Verify that insecure protocols no longer respond

steps.description: Configure NTP with authenticated time sources for accurate and trustworthy timestamps.

outputs.name: ntp-config
outputs.desc: NTP configuration with authenticated time sources

outputs.name: time-sync-status
outputs.desc: Verification that all devices are synchronized

process: Configure at least two NTP servers with authentication keys
Disable NTP as a server on devices that should only be clients
Verify time synchronization status on each device
Set the timezone consistently across all devices

steps.description: Produce the network device hardening report summarizing all changes and remaining items.

outputs.name: hardening-report
outputs.desc: Full network hardening report with findings and changes

outputs.name: exception-list
outputs.desc: List of items not hardened with justification

process: Compile all change logs from each hardening step
Run a configuration compliance check against the baseline
Document any exceptions with risk acceptance justification
Produce the final report with device-by-device status

description: Harden a database server by applying patches, restricting access, enabling encryption, and configuring audit logging.

steps.description: Apply the latest security patches to the database server.

inputs.name: database-type
inputs.desc: Database product and version (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, etc.)

outputs.name: patch-report
outputs.desc: List of patches applied with dates

outputs.name: updated-version
outputs.desc: Database version after patching

process: Check the vendor advisory page for available security patches
Test patches in a non-production environment first
Apply the patches and restart the database service
Verify the database is operational after patching

steps.description: Remove default databases, sample schemas, and default accounts.

outputs.name: removed-defaults
outputs.desc: List of default items removed

outputs.name: remaining-objects
outputs.desc: Inventory of remaining databases and accounts

process: Remove or rename sample databases (test, world, sakila, scott, etc.)
Remove anonymous or default user accounts
Change the default administrator password if not already set
Verify that no default objects remain accessible

steps.description: Configure authentication and access controls to enforce least privilege.

outputs.name: access-config
outputs.desc: Applied authentication and authorization settings

outputs.name: privilege-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix of users, roles, and their granted privileges

process: Configure authentication to require passwords or certificate-based login
Create roles matching application requirements with minimum necessary privileges
Revoke unnecessary privileges from existing accounts
Restrict administrative access to named accounts only

steps.description: Enable encryption for data in transit (TLS) and at rest (TDE or filesystem encryption).

outputs.name: encryption-config
outputs.desc: Applied encryption settings for transit and rest

outputs.name: certificate-info
outputs.desc: TLS certificate details and expiration date

process: Generate or install a TLS certificate for the database listener
Configure the database to require TLS for all client connections
Enable transparent data encryption or filesystem-level encryption for data files
Verify encrypted connections from client applications

steps.description: Configure database audit logging to capture access and modification events.

inputs.name: privilege-matrix
inputs.desc: User and role privileges to determine what to audit

outputs.name: audit-config
outputs.desc: Applied audit logging configuration

outputs.name: audit-test-results
outputs.desc: Verification that audit events are being captured

process: Enable audit logging for login events (success and failure)
Configure auditing for DDL operations (CREATE, ALTER, DROP)
Configure auditing for privileged operations (GRANT, REVOKE)
Set log rotation and retention to meet compliance requirements

steps.description: Restrict network access to the database to only required client hosts.

outputs.name: network-config
outputs.desc: Applied network restrictions (listen address, pg_hba, firewall rules)

outputs.name: connectivity-test
outputs.desc: Results of access testing from authorized and unauthorized hosts

process: Configure the database to listen only on required interfaces
Set host-based access controls (pg_hba.conf or equivalent)
Configure firewall rules to allow database port only from application servers
Test connectivity from authorized and unauthorized source addresses

steps.description: Produce the database hardening report summarizing all changes and compliance status.

outputs.name: hardening-report
outputs.desc: Full database hardening report

outputs.name: compliance-status
outputs.desc: Compliance status against the relevant benchmark

process: Compile all change logs from each hardening step
Run a compliance scan against the CIS database benchmark
Document any accepted exceptions with justification
Produce the final report with compliance score

description: Harden a web server by disabling unnecessary modules, setting security headers, and configuring TLS.

steps.description: Disable unnecessary web server modules to reduce the attack surface.

inputs.name: application-requirements
inputs.desc: Modules required by the hosted application

outputs.name: module-config
outputs.desc: List of enabled and disabled modules

outputs.name: module-change-log
outputs.desc: Record of modules disabled

process: List all currently enabled modules
Compare against the application requirements to identify unnecessary modules
Disable each unnecessary module
Restart the web server and verify the application still functions

steps.description: Configure security response headers to protect against common web attacks.

outputs.name: header-config
outputs.desc: Applied security header configuration

outputs.name: header-test-results
outputs.desc: Verification of headers in the HTTP response

process: Configure Content-Security-Policy with appropriate source directives
Set Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) with a minimum one-year max-age
Set X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, and Referrer-Policy
Test the response headers with a browser or command-line tool

steps.description: Configure TLS with strong cipher suites and certificate settings.

outputs.name: tls-config
outputs.desc: Applied TLS configuration (protocols, ciphers, OCSP)

outputs.name: tls-test-results
outputs.desc: Results from a TLS configuration scanner

process: Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1, enable only TLS 1.2 and 1.3
Configure cipher suite preference to use AEAD ciphers first
Enable OCSP stapling for certificate validation
Test the configuration with an external TLS scanner

steps.description: Remove server version information from HTTP responses and error pages.

outputs.name: disclosure-config
outputs.desc: Configuration changes to suppress version information

outputs.name: disclosure-test
outputs.desc: Verification that version info is no longer exposed

process: Set ServerTokens to Prod (Apache) or server_tokens off (Nginx)
Configure custom error pages that do not reveal server details
Remove or modify any X-Powered-By or similar headers
Test by requesting invalid URLs and checking the response

steps.description: Configure request size limits, timeouts, and rate limiting to prevent abuse.

inputs.name: application-requirements
inputs.desc: Maximum expected request sizes and rates

outputs.name: limit-config
outputs.desc: Applied request limits and timeout settings

outputs.name: limit-test-results
outputs.desc: Verification that oversized or excessive requests are rejected

process: Set maximum request body size based on application needs
Configure connection and request timeouts
Set up rate limiting per IP address or authentication token
Test with oversized and high-volume requests to verify enforcement

steps.description: Set file and directory permissions for the web root to prevent unauthorized modification.

inputs.name: module-config
inputs.desc: Enabled modules to determine which directories need write access

outputs.name: permission-config
outputs.desc: Applied file and directory permissions

outputs.name: permission-change-log
outputs.desc: Record of permission changes

process: Set the web root ownership to a non-root user
Remove write permissions from static content directories
Restrict access to configuration files (readable only by the web server user)
Disable directory listing

steps.description: Produce the web server hardening report with all changes and test results.

outputs.name: hardening-report
outputs.desc: Full web server hardening report

outputs.name: compliance-score
outputs.desc: TLS grade and header compliance score

process: Compile all change logs and test results
Run a final scan (SSL Labs, securityheaders.com equivalent checks)
Document any exceptions with justification
Produce the report with the compliance grade

description: Harden an email server by configuring authentication protocols, encryption, and anti-abuse controls.

steps.description: Configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records for email authentication.

inputs.name: mail-server-ip
inputs.desc: IP addresses of authorized mail servers

outputs.name: dns-records
outputs.desc: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC DNS records to publish

outputs.name: dkim-keys
outputs.desc: DKIM signing keys generated for the domain

process: Create the SPF TXT record listing all authorized sending IPs
Generate DKIM signing keys and publish the public key as a DNS TXT record
Create the DMARC record starting with p=none for monitoring, then tightening to quarantine or reject
Verify all three records resolve correctly from external DNS

steps.description: Enable TLS encryption for all email connections (STARTTLS and MTA-STS).

outputs.name: tls-config
outputs.desc: Applied TLS configuration for the mail server

outputs.name: mta-sts-policy
outputs.desc: MTA-STS policy published for the domain

process: Install a valid TLS certificate on the mail server
Enable STARTTLS for SMTP, IMAPS, and POP3S
Publish an MTA-STS policy to require TLS from sending servers
Test encrypted delivery with external mail servers

steps.description: Disable open relay and restrict mail relay to authorized users and networks.

outputs.name: relay-config
outputs.desc: Applied relay restriction settings

outputs.name: relay-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of open relay testing from external sources

process: Configure the mail server to reject relay from unauthenticated sources
Set the mynetworks or equivalent to include only trusted subnets
Require SMTP authentication for outbound relay
Test for open relay from an external IP address

steps.description: Configure anti-spam and anti-malware scanning for inbound and outbound mail.

outputs.name: antispam-config
outputs.desc: Applied anti-spam and anti-malware settings

outputs.name: filter-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of test messages through the filters

process: Configure spam filtering (SpamAssassin, rspamd, or equivalent)
Configure antivirus scanning (ClamAV or equivalent)
Set up DNSBL checks against known spam sources
Test with EICAR test files and known spam patterns

steps.description: Set message size limits and rate controls to prevent abuse.

outputs.name: limit-config
outputs.desc: Applied message size and rate limits

outputs.name: limit-test-results
outputs.desc: Verification that limits are enforced

process: Set maximum message size (including attachments)
Configure per-user and per-IP sending rate limits
Set maximum recipients per message
Test enforcement with oversized messages and rapid sending

steps.description: Configure authentication requirements for mail access and sending.

outputs.name: auth-config
outputs.desc: Applied authentication configuration

outputs.name: auth-test-results
outputs.desc: Verification that unauthenticated access is denied

process: Require authentication for IMAP and POP3 access
Require SMTP AUTH for message submission
Disable plaintext authentication mechanisms (allow only encrypted)
Test that unauthenticated access is rejected

steps.description: Produce the email server hardening report with all configuration changes and test results.

outputs.name: hardening-report
outputs.desc: Full email server hardening report

outputs.name: compliance-summary
outputs.desc: Summary of SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and TLS compliance

process: Compile all configuration changes and test results
Run an external email security check (MXToolbox or equivalent)
Document any exceptions with justification
Produce the report with compliance status for each control

description: Create and apply a security hardening baseline for endpoint workstations.

steps.description: Enable full disk encryption on the endpoint.

inputs.name: encryption-policy
inputs.desc: Organization encryption requirements and key escrow settings

outputs.name: encryption-status
outputs.desc: Disk encryption status and recovery key location

outputs.name: encryption-config
outputs.desc: Applied encryption settings (BitLocker, FileVault, LUKS)

process: Check if full disk encryption is already enabled
Enable BitLocker (Windows), FileVault (macOS), or LUKS (Linux)
Escrow the recovery key to the designated management system
Verify the disk is fully encrypted

steps.description: Configure the host firewall to restrict inbound connections.

outputs.name: firewall-config
outputs.desc: Applied host firewall rules

outputs.name: firewall-test-results
outputs.desc: Verification that unauthorized connections are blocked

process: Enable the host firewall if not already active
Set the default inbound policy to block
Allow only required inbound services (if any)
Test that remote connections to non-allowed ports are rejected

steps.description: Configure application whitelisting or control policies to prevent unauthorized software execution.

inputs.name: approved-applications
inputs.desc: List of approved applications and their publishers

outputs.name: whitelist-config
outputs.desc: Applied application control policy

outputs.name: whitelist-test-results
outputs.desc: Verification that unauthorized executables are blocked

process: Configure AppLocker (Windows), Santa (macOS), or fapolicyd (Linux)
Create rules allowing approved applications by publisher or hash
Set the policy to enforce mode
Test that an unauthorized executable is blocked

steps.description: Configure automatic patching for the operating system and applications.

outputs.name: patch-config
outputs.desc: Applied automatic update settings

outputs.name: patch-status
outputs.desc: Current patch compliance status

process: Configure Windows Update, Software Update, or unattended-upgrades
Set a maintenance window for automatic restarts if required
Check current patch compliance
Configure third-party application patching if applicable

steps.description: Disable autorun for removable media and restrict USB device usage if required.

outputs.name: autorun-config
outputs.desc: Applied autorun and removable media settings

outputs.name: usb-policy
outputs.desc: Applied USB device control policy

process: Disable autorun and autoplay for all drive types
Configure USB device class restrictions if required by policy
Test that inserting removable media does not auto-execute content

steps.description: Install and configure endpoint detection and response (EDR) software.

outputs.name: edr-status
outputs.desc: EDR installation and enrollment status

outputs.name: edr-config
outputs.desc: Applied EDR policy settings

process: Install the EDR agent and enroll with the management console
Configure the detection policy (prevention mode vs detect-only)
Verify the agent is reporting to the console
Test detection with a benign test sample (EICAR or equivalent)

steps.description: Produce the endpoint hardening baseline document with all applied settings.

outputs.name: baseline-document
outputs.desc: Complete endpoint hardening baseline with all settings

outputs.name: compliance-checklist
outputs.desc: Checklist for verifying baseline compliance on other endpoints

process: Compile all configuration settings into the baseline document
Create a checklist for verifying each control on a new endpoint
Document any platform-specific variations
Produce the baseline document and compliance checklist

description: Harden a cloud account (AWS, Azure, or GCP) by configuring identity, logging, and security services.

steps.description: Enable multi-factor authentication on the root or global admin account.

outputs.name: mfa-status
outputs.desc: MFA enrollment status for root and admin accounts

outputs.name: mfa-config
outputs.desc: MFA settings applied

process: Identify the root or global admin account
Enable MFA using a hardware token or authenticator application
Verify MFA is required for console login
Store the MFA recovery codes in a secure location

steps.description: Configure billing alerts to detect unexpected spending from compromised credentials.

inputs.name: budget-threshold
inputs.desc: Monthly budget amount and alert thresholds

outputs.name: billing-alerts
outputs.desc: Configured billing alert rules

outputs.name: notification-config
outputs.desc: Alert notification targets (email, SMS, webhook)

process: Set a monthly budget based on expected usage
Configure alerts at 50%, 80%, and 100% of the budget
Set up anomaly detection for spending spikes
Verify alert delivery to the designated recipients

steps.description: Enable audit logging for all API calls and management plane activity.

outputs.name: audit-log-config
outputs.desc: Applied audit logging configuration

outputs.name: log-storage
outputs.desc: Log destination bucket or workspace with retention settings

process: Enable CloudTrail (AWS), Activity Log (Azure), or Audit Log (GCP)
Configure log storage in a dedicated bucket with versioning and encryption
Set log retention to meet compliance requirements
Verify that a test API call generates an audit log entry

steps.description: Create a break-glass account for emergency access when the primary admin is unavailable.

inputs.name: mfa-status
inputs.desc: MFA already configured on the primary admin

outputs.name: breakglass-account
outputs.desc: Break-glass account details (stored securely)

outputs.name: breakglass-procedure
outputs.desc: Documented procedure for using the break-glass account

process: Create a dedicated break-glass account with admin privileges
Configure MFA with a separately stored hardware token
Set up alerting for any use of the break-glass account
Document the procedure and store credentials in a physical safe or secrets vault

steps.description: Apply least-privilege IAM policies to all users and service accounts.

inputs.name: audit-log-config
inputs.desc: Audit logging to monitor IAM changes

outputs.name: iam-policies
outputs.desc: Applied IAM policies with their scope

outputs.name: iam-review-log
outputs.desc: Record of privilege changes made during the review

process: Inventory all IAM users, groups, roles, and service accounts
Remove unused accounts and access keys
Apply least-privilege policies based on actual usage (use access analyzer tools)
Enforce a maximum key age and rotation policy

steps.description: Enable the cloud provider's security monitoring services.

outputs.name: security-services
outputs.desc: Enabled security services and their configuration

outputs.name: alert-config
outputs.desc: Alert routing for security findings

process: Enable GuardDuty (AWS), Defender for Cloud (Azure), or Security Command Center (GCP)
Configure threat detection for the account and all regions
Set up alert routing to the security operations team
Review initial findings and address any critical items

steps.description: Produce the cloud account hardening report with all configurations and compliance status.

outputs.name: hardening-report
outputs.desc: Full cloud account hardening report

outputs.name: cis-compliance-score
outputs.desc: Compliance score against the CIS cloud benchmark

process: Run the CIS cloud benchmark assessment
Compile all configuration changes and their justification

description: Harden wireless network infrastructure by configuring encryption, segmentation, and monitoring.

steps.description: Configure WPA3 or WPA2-Enterprise with RADIUS authentication on access points.

inputs.name: ap-inventory
inputs.desc: List of access points with model and firmware version

inputs.name: auth-method
inputs.desc: Authentication method (WPA3-Enterprise, WPA2-Enterprise with RADIUS, or WPA3-Personal)

outputs.name: wireless-auth-config
outputs.desc: Applied wireless authentication settings per SSID

outputs.name: radius-config

outputs.name: wps-change-log
outputs.desc: Record of WPS configuration changes

process: Check WPS status on each access point
Disable WPS PIN method and push-button method

steps.description: Set strong pre-shared keys where PSK authentication is required (guest or IoT networks).

process: Generate a strong random passphrase (minimum 20 characters) for each PSK SSID
Apply the new PSK to all access points broadcasting that SSID
Document the PSK rotation schedule (quarterly or on personnel change)
Test connectivity with the new PSK

steps.description: Segment wireless traffic into separate VLANs to isolate corporate, guest, and IoT devices.

outputs.desc: VLAN assignments per SSID

outputs.name: segmentation-test
outputs.desc: Verification that inter-VLAN traffic is blocked where intended

process: Assign each SSID to a dedicated VLAN
Configure ACLs or firewall rules to restrict guest and IoT VLANs from the corporate network
Allow only internet access from the guest VLAN
Test that devices on one VLAN cannot reach devices on a restricted VLAN

steps.description: Control SSID broadcast settings based on network sensitivity.

outputs.name: ssid-broadcast-config
outputs.desc: Broadcast settings per SSID

outputs.name: hidden-ssid-list
outputs.desc: List of hidden SSIDs and their connection instructions

process: Disable SSID broadcast for management or sensitive networks
Keep the guest SSID visible for usability
Document the hidden SSID connection procedure for authorized users

steps.description: Configure wireless intrusion detection and prevention to identify rogue access points.

inputs.name: ssid-broadcast-config
inputs.desc: Broadcast settings to identify expected SSIDs
